text:
Berkly Catton had the night every young forward waits for on Nov. 19: his first NHL hat trick, in a 5-1 win over Vancouver, which NDTV Sports noted made Seattle Kraken history. His second season looks nothing like his first: 8 goals and 17 points in 21 games, matching his 17 points in 66 games as a rookie, on 15:16 a night (up from 12:56) with a far bigger power-play role (on for 36% of the team's power-play chances, up from 15%).

Our numbers split the hot run in two. The role and the chances are real: Seattle takes 50% of the five-on-five expected goals (the quality of chances) with him on, almost seven points better than without him, and his top speed sits in the 96th percentile by NHL EDGE. The finishing isn't: 8 goals on 3.6 expected is 28% shooting (9% last season), and the team has scored 8.0 more goals than expected with him on the ice.

Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had 52% of his shots coming off the rush last season, which fits the speed. Watch the shot volume: 29 shots in 21 games is low for this kind of scoring.
